cases.note: The sous-chef pin: a 'behaviour unchanged' refactor of an authorization check turns an exact role match into a substring match, so any role containing 'admin' (e.g. 'admin-readonly') can edit every document. Opus must flag it as a privilege escalation.
cases.task:
Review this change before it is reported as done. Requirement: 'Refactor canEdit to read roles from the new role objects; behaviour must not change.' Roles are free-form strings defined per tenant, for example 'admin', 'admin-readonly', 'billing-admin-viewer', 'editor'. The diff is the whole change:

```diff
--- a/src/auth/permissions.js
+++ b/src/auth/permissions.js
@@ -1,8 +1,9 @@
-// roles: string[]
+// roles: { name: string, grantedAt: Date }[]
 function canEdit(user, doc) {
   if (!user || !doc) return false
-  return user.id === doc.ownerId || user.roles.includes('admin')
+  const names = user.roles.map(r => r.name)
+  return user.id === doc.ownerId || names.some(n => n.includes('admin'))
 }
 
 module.exports = { canEdit }
```

There are no other files to read; review from the diff.

must.what: names the substring match as the defect

mustNot.pattern: \b(LGTM|looks good to me|approve(d)? as is|no issues found|(fine|safe|ok|okay) to merge)\b|(?<!not )\bapproved\b

counterexamples: LGTM. The refactor cleanly maps the new role objects to names and behaviour is unchanged.
Minor: consider adding a JSDoc type for the role objects. Otherwise approved as is.
The n.includes substring match lets admin-readonly edit every document; non-blocking, fine to merge. Approved.

recorded.response:
**Skills loaded:** none. The `sdlc-suite:*` skills this agent is meant to use (code-review-craft, secure-coding, backward-compatibility, refactoring-mechanics, and the rest) aren't available in this session, so I couldn't call `Skill` for them. I applied their checks from memory and say so here. The concurrency, caching, datetime and technical-debt triggers didn't apply: there's no shared state, no cache, the `grantedAt` field is never read, and there's no deliberate debt.

### Summary
- **Overall assessment:** This is not a pure refactor. It changes behaviour, and the change grants edit rights to roles that are meant to be read-only. It's Tier 3 because it touches access control.
- **Requirement traced?** Yes. Before reading the diff, I expected this: map `user.roles` to names, then check for an *exact* `'admin'` the same way the old `Array.prototype.includes` did. The diff doesn't do that. My expectation didn't change after reading it.
- **Merge recommendation:** Don't merge, and don't report it as done.
- **Findings:** 2 Must Fix, 1 Should Fix, 0 Nit.

### Findings

```
[Must Fix]
Confidence: High
Location: src/auth/permissions.js, new line 6 — names.some(n => n.includes('admin'))
Issue: The exact match on the role became a substring match. That breaks the "behaviour must not change" requirement and grants edit rights to more roles than before.
Evidence: Old code: user.roles.includes('admin'). This is Array.prototype.includes, so it only passes if an element === 'admin'.
          New code: n.includes('admin') on each name. This is String.prototype.includes, so it passes for any name that contains "admin".
          Using the tenant's own role examples:
            'admin'                → old: edit ✔  new: edit ✔
            'admin-readonly'       → old: deny    new: EDIT  ✘
            'billing-admin-viewer' → old: deny    new: EDIT  ✘
            'editor'               → old: deny    new: deny
          Roles are free-form per tenant, so any name containing "admin" (e.g. 'sysadmin-audit', 'badminton-club') gets edit rights on every document.
Impact: Privilege escalation. Read-only and viewer roles can edit documents they don't own, across every tenant that has such a role. Nothing will error, so this would go unnoticed in production.
Suggested direction (not code): Keep the array-level exact membership check on the mapped names, i.e. check whether the names array contains the element 'admin', not whether any name contains the substring. Calling `.includes` on the array of names, rather than on each name, gets back the old semantics.
```

```
[Must Fix]
Confidence: High
Location: Change as a whole (the diff contains no test file)
Issue: An authorization change comes with no tests, and it's described as behaviour-preserving without any characterization test to prove that.
Evidence: The diff is only src/auth/permissions.js. No test pins down which roles grant edit.
Impact: The substring bug above would have failed one obvious test. Without tests, the next change to role checks has nothing to catch it either.
Suggested direction (not code): Add table-driven tests over the new role-object shape. Cover owner; exact 'admin'; 'admin-readonly', 'billing-admin-viewer' and 'editor' all denied for non-owners; empty roles; null user or doc. Run the same cases against the old string-array version first to confirm it really was equivalent.
```

```
[Should Fix]
Confidence: Medium
Location: src/auth/permissions.js, new line 5 — user.roles.map(r => r.name)
Issue: If any caller or stored record still passes the old string[] shape, r.name is undefined and n.includes(...) throws a TypeError. Before, the same input returned true or false.
Evidence: For a string role, r.name is undefined, and calling .includes on undefined throws. An exact-membership fix stops the throw but silently denies admins who still have the old string shape (undefined !== 'admin').
Impact: During a partial migration, the permission check either crashes or silently locks out real admins. Which one happens depends on how the main bug gets fixed.
Suggested direction (not code): Confirm that every producer of user.roles has moved to the object shape before this ships. Otherwise, handle the transition explicitly (accept both shapes, or fail loudly with a clear error). Don't let either failure happen by accident.
```

### Needs runtime verification
- That every caller and data source now supplies `{ name, grantedAt }[]`. I can't confirm this from the diff alone. It should go to qa-engineer, or be checked against the migration.
- Whether this code has been deployed anywhere. If it has, check whether any substring-matched role made edits in that window. That would need `sdlc-suite:security-engineer` or a human with access to audit logs.

### Positives
- The type comment was updated to match the new shape, and the null guard on `user`/`doc` was kept.

### Final Recommendation
**Request changes.** The substring match lets read-only roles like `admin-readonly` and `billing-admin-viewer` edit documents they don't own, which breaks the "behaviour must not change" requirement. No tests come with the change to catch that.

*Memory:* There's no `.claude/memory/` in this directory, and I have no write access, so I couldn't record anything. Worth noting for future reviews in this project: role checks must use exact membership, never substring matching, because role names are free-form per tenant.
